items.label: Band gap of Si (300 K)
items.note: Sets silicon's absorption edge near 1.1 µm.

items.label: Band gap of Ge (room temp.)
items.note: Absorption edge near 1.9 µm, useful for infrared detection.

items.label: Band gap of GaAs (room temp.)
items.note: A direct gap; GaAs emits near-infrared light at about 870 nm.

items.label: Band gap of SiC / GaN
items.note: 4H-SiC, the power-device polytype, is about 3.26 eV.

items.label: Thermal voltage kT/q (300 K)
items.note: Precisely about 0.0259 V at 300 K.

items.label: Intrinsic density ni of Si (room temp.)
items.note: Sources quote 1.0–1.5×10¹⁰ cm⁻³.

items.label: Electron / hole mobility in Si
items.note: Lightly doped silicon at room temperature; electrons are about three times faster.

items.label: Lattice constant of Si
items.note: Diamond-structure cubic cell holding eight atoms.

items.label: Atomic density of Si
items.note: A 1×10¹⁶ cm⁻³ dopant level is one atom in five million.

items.label: Photon energy vs. wavelength
items.note: GaN's 3.4 eV corresponds to about 365 nm.

items.label: Subthreshold swing limit (room temp.)
items.note: Lowering Vth by ΔV multiplies subthreshold current by 10^(ΔV/S); at the ideal 60 mV/dec, 60 mV gives 10×.

items.label: Threshold voltage, advanced logic
items.note: With other conditions fixed, 0.1 V lower Vth raises subthreshold current by 10^(0.1 V / S): about 18× at S = 80 mV/dec.

items.label: Gate EOT, advanced devices
items.note: Includes the interfacial layer; measured CET is somewhat larger.

items.label: Relative permittivity: SiO₂ / HfO₂
items.note: SiON is about 5–6 and Si3N4 about 7.

items.label: Breakdown field of thermal SiO₂
items.note: Devices run at a few MV/cm or less to last ten years.

items.label: Si diode forward voltage / BJT VBE
items.note: Voltage at which a practical (mA-level) current flows at room temperature.

items.label: Diode VF / VBE temperature coefficient
items.note: At constant current; used in on-chip temperature sensors.

items.label: Ideal SNR of an N-bit ADC (full-scale sine)
items.note: Quantization noise only, integrated from DC to fs/2. About 74 dB at 12 bits and 98 dB at 16 bits.

items.label: DRAM refresh window (DDR4, 0–85 °C)
items.note: Every row is refreshed within this window; 32 ms at 85–95 °C. DDR5 uses 32 ms (16 ms when hot). Average command spacing tREFI ≈ 7.8 µs for DDR4.

items.label: DRAM cell capacitance
items.note: 0 and 1 differ by only tens of thousands of electrons.

items.label: Cell area: DRAM 1T1C vs. 6T SRAM
items.note: DRAM packs roughly 20 times denser.

items.label: NAND flash endurance (P/E cycles)
items.value: SLC ≈ 100,000 · TLC a few thousand · QLC ≈ 1,000

items.label: Flash data retention (example)
items.note: Depends on product, wear and temperature: one SSD is rated 10 years at beginning of life but 1 year at end of life (25 °C).

items.label: EUV wavelength
items.note: About 92 eV per photon, roughly 14 times ArF's photon energy.

items.label: EUV numerical aperture
items.note: High-NA improves resolution about 1.7×.

items.label: Standard wafer diameter / thickness
items.note: A 300 mm wafer weighs about 128 g.

items.label: ISO Class 5 cleanroom limit
items.note: Each class step is a factor of 10; room air is around Class 9.

items.label: Melting point of Si
items.note: Thermal oxidation runs at about 800–1,200 °C.

items.label: Front-end cycle time, leading-edge logic
items.note: Over a thousand process steps.

items.label: L1 cache hit
items.note: Capacity: tens of KB.

items.label: L2 cache hit
items.note: L3 takes over ten ns (tens of cycles).

items.label: DRAM (main memory) access
items.note: Hundreds of cycles for a CPU running at several GHz.

items.label: HDD access
items.note: Seek plus rotational delay; SSD random access is hundreds of times faster.

items.label: Cache line size
items.note: One DDR4 BL8 burst on a 64-bit channel: 8 transfers × 8 bytes, excluding ECC.

items.label: Page size / huge page (x86-64)
items.note: A 64-entry TLB would cover 256 KiB with 4 KiB pages or 128 MiB with 2 MiB pages; real TLB sizes differ by design.

items.label: CTE: Si vs. organic substrate
items.note: Glass/epoxy laminate below Tg; through-thickness CTE is much larger and low-CTE package laminates are lower. Si is about 2.6×10⁻⁶ /K.

items.label: Pitch: microbumps vs. hybrid bonding
items.value: typically tens of µm vs. < 10 µm
items.note: Microbump pitches near 10 µm have been shown in research. Connection count scales with 1/pitch².

items.label: HBM3 bandwidth per stack
items.note: 6.4 Gb/s per pin.

items.label: PCIe per-lane rate, Gen 3 → Gen 6
items.note: Roughly doubles each generation.

items.label: Typical design-life target
items.note: Always tied to a stated junction temperature and duty cycle, e.g. 10 years continuous at Tj = 105 °C for some industrial processors.

items.label: Temperature rule of thumb
items.note: Holds roughly near room temperature for Ea ≈ 0.5 eV.

items.label: ESD robustness target (human body model)
items.note: Industry bodies now recommend 1 kV HBM for many ICs with proper ESD controls; use the device's qualification rating.

items.label: Max junction temp., Si power devices
items.note: Designs typically operate around 125 °C for margin.

items.label: CMOS dynamic power
items.note: Halving the supply voltage cuts dynamic power to a quarter.
